description:
ts_elixir's Tailscale.Tcp.Stream.recv/1 returns whatever data is available with no length parameter.
gen_tcp's recv/3 takes (socket, length, timeout) where length=0 means "return available" and length>0 means "return exactly N bytes".

Options:
1. Add recv/2 (stream, max_bytes) to ts_elixir NIF — Rust side reads up to N bytes
2. Add recv/3 (stream, max_bytes, timeout) — with timeout support
3. Handle buffering entirely in Elixir (works but less efficient — double copy)

Preferred: option 2 if feasible in tailscale-rs, otherwise option 3 as fallback.
File upstream PR against https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-rs

comments.text:
Change committed on branch pm/tcp-recv-max-len in ~/src/tailscale-rs.
4 files, 38 lines added:
- tcp.rs: new tcp_recv_max NIF using TcpStream::recv(&mut buf) with sized buffer
- native.ex: tcp_recv_max/2 NIF stub
- stream.ex: recv/2 public API (max_bytes=0 falls back to recv/1)
- erlang.ex: recv/2 erlang re-export

The underlying TcpStream::recv already supports max_len — it was just
not exposed through the NIF. No changes needed to tailscale-rs core.

Ready to push and open a PR against tailscale/tailscale-rs.
Pushed to fork: Munksgaard/tailscale-rs branch pm/tcp-recv-max-len. PR not opened yet.
